dm4.name: Central bank gold buying, last 4 quarters
dm4.source: World Gold Council Gold Demand Trends (quarterly; typed in)
dm4.measured_against: the 4 quarters before, both on WGC's latest published figure for each quarter
dm4.what: How much gold the world's central banks bought in the last 12 months vs the 12 months before.
dm4.why: Central banks have been gold's steadiest buyer since 2022 and buy regardless of interest rates; their pace sets a floor under the price.
dm4.bull_means: Central banks are buying faster: the floor under gold is rising.
dm4.bear_means: Central banks are buying less: weaker support if other buyers step back.
dm4._weight_note: Half weight (12 -> 6) until WGC's Q3 2026 report (~29 Oct) because WGC reclassified 187 t of Q1 2026 central-bank buying; Kenneth, 1 Oct 2026. Revisit then: back to 12 if the trend is confirmed.

dm5.name: Consumer demand: jewellery plus bars and coins
dm5.source: World Gold Council Gold Demand Trends (quarterly; typed in)
dm5.measured_against: same quarter a year earlier, in tonnes
dm5.what: Tonnes of gold bought as jewellery and as bars and coins (mostly China and India) vs the same quarter a year earlier.
dm5.why: Shows whether everyday buyers still take metal at today's price; in tonnes, so high prices themselves push it down.
dm5.bull_means: Consumers are buying more metal despite the price.
dm5.bear_means: Consumers are buying less metal: the price is rationing demand.
